passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Lodging and meals on personal days are not reimbursed. For example, if you attend meetings at another office for three days and stay on for a few days of vacation, Ridgeline reimburses lodging and meals for the business days within the limits in §4 and §5.1, and airfare up to the business-only comparison fare. Lodging and meals for the vacation days are yours, and the vacation days are PTO.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: While travelling on business, meals are reimbursed up to $75 per day for domestic travel and up to $90 per day for international travel. Any amount over the daily cap is not reimbursed. The daily cap covers all your meals that day together, including tips. Domestic means travel within your own country; international means travel outside it. For example, a single dinner costing more than the domestic daily cap on a site visit is reimbursed only up to the cap, and you pay the difference. Meals provided by a client or included in a conference fee are not claimed again.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: When you combine business and personal travel, airfare is reimbursed up to the business-only comparison fare, which Ridgeline Travel quotes at booking for the dates the business trip alone would need.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Hotel lodging is reimbursed up to $250 per night in the US and up to $275 per night outside the US (international), before taxes. Book through Ridgeline Travel. The nightly limit depends on where you stay, not where you are from: a Denver employee staying in Toronto uses the international limit. If no reasonable hotel is available within the limit, for example during a major event, ask your manager to approve the higher rate before booking and note the approval on your claim. Room service, minibar and in-room entertainment are personal costs.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Client entertainment, such as a meal with a client, is reimbursed up to $100 per person and needs your manager's pre-approval. On your claim, list the people attended, their organisations and the business purpose. Entertainment for public officials needs extra care; check with your manager first. Gifts and hospitality you receive from others are covered by RSE-HB-01 §4.3.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Personal days added to a business trip are taken as PTO under the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01).

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.section_heading: Adding personal days to a trip
passages.text:
You may add personal days to a business trip. Personal days are taken as PTO under the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), and the costs of the personal days are yours (RSE-EXP-01 §6).
Request the PTO in the usual way, with the usual notice and approval. Your holiday calendar is still your home office's calendar while you travel. Adding a few personal days doesn't turn a business trip into temporary remote work, provided you don't work on those days.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Lodging and meals on personal days are not reimbursed. For example, if you attend meetings at another office for three days and stay on for a few days of vacation, Ridgeline reimburses lodging and meals for the business days within the limits in §4 and §5.1, and airfare up to the business-only comparison fare. Lodging and meals for the vacation days are yours, and the vacation days are PTO.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Your manager must pre-approve every business trip before you book it.
Ask for approval with the purpose of the trip, the dates, the destination and an estimate of the main costs. Approval covers the business part of the trip; personal days added to it are requested separately as PTO (§2.4).

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: When you combine business and personal travel, airfare is reimbursed up to the business-only comparison fare, which Ridgeline Travel quotes at booking for the dates the business trip alone would need.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Requests for more than 3 PTO days need at least 14 calendar days' notice (two weeks) before the first day off. Requests of 3 PTO days or fewer have no minimum notice: submit them as early as practical. Count only the PTO days charged, not weekends or company holidays.
Notice is counted from the day you submit the request to the first day off. For example, a request submitted on a Monday for a full working week off starting two Mondays later meets the notice rule; the same request submitted the Friday before does not. A late request is not automatically declined, but your manager may decline it if the team can't cover your work.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
You can cancel or change a request in the HR Portal. Approved PTO that you cancel before it starts is restored to your balance.
To extend approved PTO, submit a new request for the extra days; the notice and approval rules apply to the whole absence. If you need to come back early, tell your manager and change the request so the unused days are restored.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Your manager approves your PTO requests. A request for more than 10 consecutive PTO days must also be approved by your director. See the Approval Matrix (RSE-APR-01 §2).
Consecutive PTO days are counted as PTO days charged in one continuous absence; weekends and company holidays inside the absence don't count toward the total but don't break it either. Approvers consider project needs and team cover, and they should respond promptly so you can make plans.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Submit every PTO request in the HR Portal before the first day off. Tell your team and update your calendar once it is approved.
It helps to talk to your manager before submitting a longer request, especially around project deadlines or site milestones. Your request shows your dates, the PTO days charged and your remaining balance. Your manager is notified and approves or declines it in the HR Portal; you are notified of the decision. PTO is not approved until the HR Portal shows it as approved.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
PTO up to 10 consecutive days | Manager
PTO over 10 consecutive days | Director
Field-role PTO in the December blackout | Director
Floating holiday | Manager
Sick time | None (notify your manager)
Parental, bereavement, jury duty | HR (manager notified)
Unpaid personal leave | HR
The rules behind these rows are in the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), the Holiday Calendar & Observance policy (RSE-HOL-01) and the Leave of Absence Policy (RSE-LV-01). For example, a PTO request of 11 consecutive working days needs the director, while a request of 10 or fewer needs only the manager.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Field/site-based employees may not take PTO during the last two weeks of December, from December 18 to December 31, because of year-end site work. A field/site-based employee who needs PTO in that window must get a director's exception; the request goes to the director for approval.
Company holidays in the window, such as Christmas Day, are still company holidays. The blackout does not apply to office-hybrid or remote-approved employees, whose December PTO follows the normal rules. Field/site-based employees planning December time off should talk to their manager and director early in the autumn.

The rules behind these rows are in the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), the Holiday Calendar & Observance policy (RSE-HOL-01) and the Leave of Absence Policy (RSE-LV-01). For example, a PTO request of 11 consecutive working days needs the director, while a request of 10 or fewer needs only the manager.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
If you are on approved leave that spans December 31, you can carry over up to 10 unused PTO days instead of 5.
This applies to approved leave under the Leave of Absence Policy, such as parental leave, that is in progress on December 31. It is applied automatically when your leave is recorded in the HR Portal; you don't need to request it.

passages.title: Paid Time Off Policy
passages.text:
Your PTO balance cannot go negative. You can only take PTO you have already accrued. If your request is longer than your available balance, you can reduce the request, or request unpaid personal leave for the remainder (RSE-LV-01 §6).
The HR Portal will not let you submit a request that takes your balance below zero. Managers cannot approve PTO that hasn't accrued yet, and Ridgeline does not advance PTO from future pay periods. If you are short of PTO for an important reason, talk to your manager and HR early; unpaid personal leave is approved by HR.

passages.title: Holiday Calendar & Observance
passages.text:
Part-time employees are paid for a company holiday if it falls on one of their scheduled working days. Field/site-based employees who are asked to work on a company holiday get a substitute day off within 30 calendar days, agreed with their manager.
A part-time employee whose scheduled days don't include the holiday is not given another day off in its place. Substitute days for field staff are recorded in the HR Portal and are not deducted from PTO; if the substitute day isn't taken within the window, talk to your manager and HR.

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns about coverage.

Maya
